business_type_notes: Every category is A (the calibration pack, section 2): a job is quoted per surface, booked once and done in a visit, and the customer comes back when the growth returns, not on a round. The split inside A is written into the briefs, not the type: problem led pages (soft washing, roof, render, cladding, driveway and patio, brick and stone, decking, oil and rust stains, graffiti, fascia and soffit, conservatory) read block 4 as symptom, cause and consequence; schedule led pages (block paving and concrete sealing, solar panel cleaning, and commercial cleaning where the client confirms planned visits) read the 'on a schedule led page' line in each brief, what slips and when; the commercial pages (car park, tennis court and sports surface, industrial and warehouse) read the 'on a commercial page' line, the symptom in use and what it costs the site. The pack's only desire led case (a clean before a sale or an event) is a situation line inside the briefs, because no page target is desire led: no page is flagged in the library and there is no desire variant. The Window Cleaning Service and Gutter Cleaning Service tabs are not in the pack's section 2 table and take the default. steps.title: Tell Us Which Surfaces Need Cleaning
steps.brief: How to get in touch and what is useful to send first (which surfaces, a rough size, a photo of the growth or the stain, whether there is an outside tap and where the water runs to). No promise of a reply time unless [CV: response_time] is set.

steps.title: We Look at the Surface and Price the Job
steps.brief: The visit and what gets looked at: what the surface is made of and how it is finished, how much growth or staining it carries, the state of the joints or the pointing, height and access, where the wash water will go. Follows [CV: quote_method]; only say the quote is written if quote_method says so. Never restates 'free' (FAQ 5 owns it). Never a pressure, a product or a dwell time as this client's method.

steps.title: We Clean on a Date That Suits You
steps.brief: The date is agreed in advance, to suit the customer. The weather only as the reason a date can move, from the trade facts timing cells (wet cleaning of walls and paving is held off when frost threatens; a treatment and a sealer need a dry surface), and only when the weather_delays_rebooked practice is confirmed. Never mention the price, the quote or changes to the plan (step 2 and Why choose us own them). Never restates the start time (FAQ 4 owns it).

step_2_no_visit.title: We Price Your Job

Describe how the price is reached only from [CV: quote_method]; when quote_method is blank, name no method at all (no photos, call, video or visit). Only say the quote is written if quote_method says so. Never restates 'free' (FAQ 5 owns it).

faq_slots.question: Do you guarantee your work?

Never a promise that the growth will not return or that a stain is gone; never written as something that replaces the customer's rights (the trade facts no damage guarantee row).

faq_slots.question: What happens if something isn't right after the clean?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Used when nothing in cover_chain other than insurance is confirmed. Open with what the customer does: tell us what isn't right and we'll look at it. Then the 'reasonable care and skill' standard every trade works to, as the standard the work is held to, never as a defence. No promise to come back or put it right for free. Never invent a guarantee.

faq_slots.question: How soon can you start?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: start_time] only, as given. The weather as a reason a booking can move only from the trade facts timing cells (frost, a surface that has to be dry for a treatment or a sealer) and never as an excuse in advance. Never a same day claim unless [CV: same_day_available] is yes.

faq_slots.question: Is the quote free and no obligation?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [QUOTE_FREE] and [CV: quote_method].

faq_slots.question: How do your quotes work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: quote_method] only.

faq_slots.question: How long will my drive or patio stay clean?
faq_slots.answer_brief: No promise of a time. What decides it, in plain words: how much shade and damp the surface sits in, trees and a north facing side, and whether the growth was treated or only knocked off the top (the trade facts soft washing rows: growth that a treatment did not reach stays and regrows). Say what slows the return (a treatment after the wash, joints refilled so they hold less water) as the principle of good work, never as this client's process unless [CV: materials_methods] or a practice confirms it. Nothing about an annual clean: the facts pack gives no interval.

faq_slots.question: Why has my drive gone green again so soon after it was cleaned?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Use the assigned symptom's meaning and its linked local issue. Three genuinely different causes in plain words, from the trade facts what goes wrong rows: the top of the growth was washed off and what lives down in the pores and the joints was left to grow back; a side that never dries (shade, a tree, the north side of the house) that any surface greens on; joints washed empty, which hold water and seed. Then what the local factor adds (tree cover, a damp valley, coastal air, the housing era's surfaces), then what a proper clean has to do: treat what is left, and refill the joints. Blame the method, never the customer's effort. Never promise it stays clean.

faq_slots.question: Can a jet wash harm my paving?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Yes, when the pressure and the distance are wrong for the surface, from the trade facts facts rows: there is no one safe setting for every surface; the paving maker's guidance is a moderate pressure with the lance held at an angle and back from the surface; natural stone, including sandstone, takes a low setting because a hard jet wears it; a jet run across block joints empties them, and the sand is then brushed back in; a mortar joint that is damaged is made good. Say what a careful job does first (the surface identified, a test patch) as the principle of good work. No figure, no distance, no named product unless [CV: materials_methods] gives it.

faq_slots.question: What's the difference between a soft wash and a jet wash?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts soft washing and render rows, in plain words: a soft wash puts a treatment on at low pressure, leaves it for the time its label gives, and then rinses it off or leaves it to weather, so the growth is killed where it lives; a jet wash takes off what it hits and nothing more. Which one a surface gets is decided by the surface: render, roof tiles, soft brick, timber and painted surfaces take the low pressure route, hard concrete and block paving can take a controlled wash, and many jobs use both. Never a dilution, a dwell time or a product; a soft wash as this business's method only from [CV: materials_methods] or where the page is the Soft washing page.

faq_slots.question: Do I need permission to have my walls cleaned?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Used only when the client's services list carries brick and stone cleaning or graffiti removal. From the trade facts rule rows only, with "usually" or "in most cases": cleaning is maintenance and usually needs no building approval; a listed building is different, because consent is usually needed where the cleaning would affect what makes it special, abrasive methods most of all, and paint taken off a listed building usually needs consent first; a conservation area on its own does not stop a wall being cleaned, though controls can apply. What the customer does: the owner of a listed building asks the council before the work. Never an Act's name, never legal advice.
faq_slots.condition: the client's services list carries brick and stone cleaning or graffiti removal

faq_slots.question: Can you still clean my drive during a hosepipe ban?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts hosepipe ban rows only: a ban can cover cleaning paths, patios and walls with a hose whoever does the work, so a paid cleaner is not automatically exempt; the water company's own notice says what is and is not allowed in the area, and cleaning done for safety reasons is treated differently. Say the business checks the notice before booking in a ban, and nothing more. No promise of a way round it; never the regulation's name.

B.question: How often do planned cleaning visits need to be?
B.answer_brief: What decides it, in plain words, from the trade facts rows: how fast the dirt, the growth or the oil builds on that surface, the traffic across it, how much shade and damp it sits in, and when the site can be closed for the work. No national rule sets an interval for any surface (the cleaning frequency fact). A frequency only from [CV: visit_frequency_options]; otherwise say the pattern is agreed with the site and nothing more. Never promise a schedule.

B.question: What does a planned visit cover?
B.answer_brief: The jobs on the card list said as one visit: the bays and the walkways, the entrance, the cladding or the panels, whichever the services list has. The site kept open or closed in sections, with the wet area barriered until it is dry (the trade facts wet surfaces row) and the wash water collected, as the principle of good work. What a visit does not cover only from the services list. Link one service page where LINKABLE PAGES has one.

Methods: pressure washing with a rotary surface cleaner
After the clean: kiln dried sand brushed into block joints
Protection: wash water collected and taken off site
Access: roof moss removed from the ground or from supported access
Other: out of hours working for commercial sites
site barriered and reopened once dry

why_titles_alt: The Right Method for Every Surface

cards.title: Green and slippery by the end of winter
cards.brief: Problem led: the drive or the patio green by February, slippery when wet, a path by the back door nobody trusts in the rain, from the trade facts signs rows in the customer's words. The one cause this card makes: a surface that stays damp in the shade, where algae and moss can live in the pores and the joints. Say what the fix usually involves from the trade facts stages (the loose growth cleared, a test patch, a controlled wash, a treatment for what the wash leaves, and on block paving the joints refilled where the sand has gone), and that a wash on its own takes the top off and leaves the roots, so the treatment is the part that matters (the soft washing what goes wrong row). On a window cleaning page the card reads as green on the frames, the sills and the conservatory roof; on a gutter cleaning page as the green line below an overflowing gutter. On a commercial reading: a slippery walkway or bay and what it costs the site, never a slip figure. Where the reader is cleaning before a sale or an event, the card reads as the situation (the date, and the surfaces that show from the road), never a symptom invented for it. Never promise the growth will not return; never a pressure or a product.
cards.mechanism: a surface that stays damp in the shade

cards.title: Black spots and streaks a brush won't shift
cards.brief: Problem led: dark spots across a patio or a wall, black runs down render under the sills and below a gutter joint, from the trade facts signs rows. The one cause this card makes: growth rooted into the surface, not resting on top of it (lichen on slabs and stone, black growth on a sheltered wall). Say honestly what a clean does from the facts rows: a treatment is put on and left to work, and lichen spots then shrink and weather away over the months that follow rather than coming off on the day; a jet hard enough to take them off marks the stone first (the driveway and patio done badly row). Never name the growth from its colour alone (the render growth colours fact). On a window cleaning page the card reads as the black run down a conservatory frame and the film on the roof panels; on a gutter cleaning page as the streak under a leaking joint. Never a dwell time, never a product unless [CV: materials_methods] gives it, never a promise the spots are gone. Not the surface staying damp: card 1 owns that.
cards.mechanism: growth rooted into the surface, not resting on top of it

cards.title: Moss on the roof and in the gutters
cards.brief: Problem led, and kept in proportion: clumps of moss on the tiles, moss and silt in the gutters, water backing up at an outlet, drips down the fascia, from the trade facts roof cleaning signs row. The one cause this card makes: moss shed from the tiles and lying in the gutters where the water should run. Say first what the facts rows say: a mossy roof is rarely a problem in itself; it matters once the gutters and their downpipe openings are choked. Then the principle of good work from the roof cleaning stages: the roof looked at first to decide whether removal is needed at all, removal from the ground or from supported access rather than by walking the tiles, a treatment afterwards only where it suits the roof, the gutters cleared of what comes down. The damage the wrong method does, from the done badly row: a jet drives water into the roof and lifts the tile surface, a foot cracks a tile. On a gutter cleaning page the card leads with the gutter; on a window cleaning page it reads as the conservatory roof and its gutter. Never treat moss as an emergency; never a pressure or a product; the business's own access and method only from [CV: materials_methods].
cards.mechanism: moss shed from the tiles, choking the gutters

cards.title: Marks left by the last clean
cards.brief: The customer's real fear: stripes and arcs across a patio, joints with no sand in them and weeds coming through, a scarred patch on render that no longer matches the wall, decking gone furry, mortar raked out of a brick wall, from the trade facts done badly rows. The one cause this card makes: pressure and distance set for the machine, not for the surface. Say what the facts rows give, in plain words and with no figure: there is no one safe setting for every surface; paving makers ask for a moderate pressure with the lance angled and held back; natural stone takes a low setting because a hard jet wears it; render and roof tiles are not jetted at all. Then what a careful job does first (the surface identified, a test patch) as the principle of good work, and what is put back afterwards (joint sand brushed in, a damaged mortar joint made good). Never a dig at another trade, never that the customer did it wrong. Not the growth returning: cards 1 and 2 own that.
cards.mechanism: pressure and distance set for the machine, not the surface

Each is part of finishing the job and each adds to it; the business's own practice only from [CV: materials_methods]. Code adds the price line from [CV: price_list] when there is one.

faq_slots.question: Do you guarantee your [WORK_LOWER] work?

faq_slots.question: Are you insured for [WORK_LOWER] work?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The cover figure from [CV: insurance_cover] and what the cover is for. Never what it pays or who it covers.

faq_slots.question: What happens if something isn't right after the clean?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Open with what the customer does: tell us and we look at it. Then the reasonable care and skill standard every trade works to. No promise to come back free. Never invent a guarantee.

faq_slots.question: What does your [WORK_LOWER] work cover?
faq_slots.answer_brief: The surfaces themselves, named from the card list (drives and patios, render and walls, roofs, decking, whichever the client has), and the size of job taken on, from the services list and [CV: typical_jobs] only. Link one service page. Never 'on this page', 'listed above' or 'the card list' as words: the reader sees no list, so name the work.

faq_slots.question: What happens when I ask for a quote?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From [CV: quote_method] and the confirmed practices only: what the customer sends (which surfaces, a photo), what the business looks at (the surface, the growth, access, where the water goes), what comes back. No timescale unless [CV: response_time] is set.

faq_slots.question: When is the best time of year for [WORK_LOWER]?
faq_slots.answer_brief: From the trade facts timing cells, with the reason in the weather or the surface: most cleaning runs through the year; wet cleaning of walls and paving is held off when frost threatens, because water left in the surface freezes; a treatment needs its time to work and a sealer needs a surface that has dried, so both wait for a dry spell. Growth comes back fastest on a surface that stays damp, so a clean before the wet months is a clean that lasts into them. Nothing about spring being busy or booking ahead. No dates, no promise about the weather.

faq_symptom.frame: [SYMPTOM]: why does it happen, and what can be done?
faq_symptom.answer_brief: The symptom and its linked local issue, answered as asked. Where the symptom is a seasonal sign (a green film on the shaded side after a wet winter, moss in the gutters after autumn), say first when it is normal and then what is not, before anything else. Then the usual cause here in plain words, what the local shade, damp or housing adds (tree cover, a north facing side, a damp valley, coastal air, the surfaces the town's houses were built with), and what the business does about it. Never a claim that the town's drives or walls are dirty. One figure at most.

problem_card.title: Surfaces that never dry out in the wet months
problem_card.brief: Say first what is normal from autumn to spring: a green film on the shaded side of a drive, a patio slippery after a week of rain, moss showing in the gutters once the leaves are down, all of which any surface does when it stays damp. Then what is not: a path that is slippery all year, growth that has gone black, water backing up at an outlet. The one cause this card makes: the damp months, when nothing dries between showers and growth gets ahead. Say what gets looked at and what waits, from the trade facts timing cells: wet cleaning of walls and paving is held off when frost threatens, a treatment and a sealer wait for a dry spell. Nothing about spring being busy or booking ahead.
problem_card.mechanism: the damp months, when nothing dries between showers

faq_slot.question: Can you clean my drive or walls in winter?
faq_slot.answer_brief: What runs in the cold months and what waits, from the trade facts timing cells with the reason: a wash on hard paving runs when it is above freezing; wet cleaning of walls, brick and stone stops when frost threatens, because water left in the surface freezes and damages it; a treatment needs its time to work and a sealer a surface that has dried, so both wait for a dry spell. No dates, no temperature, no promise about the weather.

items.title: Checking what the surface is and how it's finished
items.brief: The first stage from the trade facts: the surface and its finish identified (the paving and its joints, the render and its defects, the coating on the cladding or the decking, the tiles, the panel maker's instructions), and what must not be touched. A part of the job, not a promise about the quote.

items.title: Protecting what's around it
items.brief: The protection stage from the trade facts: openings, vents, electrics, planting, ponds, cars and the neighbour's side covered or moved before any water goes on. Name only what the rows give for this service.

items.title: A test patch first
items.brief: The trial stage from the trade facts: the least forceful method tried on a small patch and the result checked before the whole surface is done. Say why, from the done badly rows; no figure.

items.title: Keeping the wash water where it should be
items.brief: The run off stage from the trade facts: drains covered or isolated, the wash water held back or collected where it carries a treatment, oil or paint, because only clean water belongs in a surface water drain (the facts row). Written as the principle of good work; the business's own practice only from [CV: materials_methods].

items.title: The clean itself
items.brief: The central stage from the trade facts, named as the trade names it for this service: a brush or a controlled wash, a treatment put on at low pressure and left for its labelled time, a hand clean, a scrub. A named method (a soft wash, a rotary cleaner, hot water) only from [CV: materials_methods]; never a pressure, a dilution or a dwell time.

items.title: Treating what the wash leaves
items.brief: The treatment stage from the trade facts: growth or a stain that is still there after the wash treated rather than jetted harder, and left to work. Honest about what fades over weeks rather than vanishing (lichen spots, oil that has gone in, a rust shadow). A product only from [CV: materials_methods].

items.title: Putting the joints and the finish back
items.brief: The reinstatement stage from the trade facts for this service: kiln dried sand brushed into block joints where the wash moved it, a mortar joint made good, the exposed edges of render looked at, the connectors on a panel left dry, the seals on a conservatory checked. Name only what the rows give.

items.title: Checking it over before we go
items.brief: The last stage from the trade facts: the surface inspected, the collected debris cleared, the gutters cleared of what came down, a commercial area reopened only once it is dry. What the customer sees when the job is done.

included.note: Fallback only: the tick items are the service's own Table A stages when the pack gives 6 or more; this set is used when it gives fewer (F-ITEMS-GENERIC).

cards.title: What you've started to notice
cards.brief: The things a homeowner notices first, from the trade facts signs row for this service, in their words: green slippery patches, black spots, weeds in the joints, tyre marks, dark patches on the decking, streaks on the fascias, a film on the roof panels, moss in the gutters. The one cause this card makes: dirt and growth the surface has held onto. Then what it leads to if left, from the skipped row (growth stays on the surface people walk on, oil goes further in, moss sits over the outlets): specific, never alarming, never a slip figure. On a schedule led page (block paving and concrete sealing, solar panel cleaning, commercial cleaning with planned visits) the card is what slips and when: a seal thinning on the turning spots and the low spots where water lies, so stains soak in again and the joints lose their sand; a film on the panels as the dirt builds, at the pace the roof's position sets; bays greasy again between visits. The reason in the surface or the weather, never in the customer's diary. On a commercial page: the symptom in use (slippery bays, moss on a court, grime on the cladding) and what it costs the site in complaints and closed areas. Where the reader is cleaning before a sale or an event, the card is the situation (the date, the surfaces that show first), never a symptom invented for it.
cards.mechanism: dirt and growth the surface has held onto

cards.title: It came back within months of the last clean
cards.brief: Green back on the drive, black patches back on the wall, within months of a wash. The one cause this card makes: growth knocked off the top with its roots left in the pores and the joints. From the trade facts soft washing rows: growth a treatment did not reach stays and regrows, and a treatment that was not left for its labelled time does the same. Say what this service does differently as the principle of good work: a treatment after the wash, left to work, so what lives in the surface is dealt with; honest that lichen spots shrink over the months rather than coming off on the day. On a schedule led page: a seal put on over an old coating that was never tested, so it did not bond and wore through early (the sealing done badly row); the old coating identified and tested first. Blame the method, never the customer's effort. Never promise it will not return; never a product unless [CV: materials_methods] gives it. Not the surface staying damp in the shade: the category page owns that.
cards.mechanism: growth knocked off the top with its roots left in the pores

cards.title: A stain that's soaked in
cards.brief: An oil patch dark in the middle of the drive, an orange rust mark under a planter or a gate, paint caught in the pores of brick, a tyre mark that a wash did not lift, from the trade facts signs rows. The one cause this card makes: a spill or a mark that went into the surface before it was dealt with. From the facts rows: oil soaks into paving, a fresh spill is soaked up rather than wiped (wiping spreads it), oil that has gone deep may lighten rather than vanish and a badly contaminated block is sometimes replaced; a rust shadow can stay; paint gets harder to shift the longer it sits. Say what the service does in plain words (the stain identified, the source stopped, a stain treatment tried on a patch, left to work, the contaminated water collected) and be honest about the result. On a growth page the card is the black lichen spot that is treated and left to fade rather than jetted. On a schedule led sealing page: stains soaking into an unsealed surface, which is what the seal is for. Never a product unless [CV: materials_methods] gives it; never promise the mark is gone.
cards.mechanism: a spill or a mark that went into the surface before it was dealt with

cards.title: Weeds and water in the joints
cards.brief: Weeds up through the block joints, sand gone from between the blocks so they rock, moss along the gaps between decking boards, dirt packed into the joints of cladding panels, debris at the conservatory gutter, from the trade facts signs rows. The one cause this card makes: joints left open, so weeds root in them and water gets in. From the facts rows: a wash across block joints takes the sand out, and kiln dried sand is brushed back into them so the blocks lock again; a damaged mortar joint is made good rather than re sanded; on render, cracks and loose patches show once the growth is off and need their own repair rather than being hidden; on cladding, dirt in the joints can hide a joint that is failing. Say what the service does at the joints as the principle of good work; the business's own practice only from [CV: materials_methods]. On a commercial page: debris at the gullies and water standing on a court. Not the pressure that emptied them: the category page owns that.
cards.mechanism: joints left open, so weeds root in them and water gets in
